variables.title: Variables
variables.notes: Variables are assigned using a colon (:). Q is a wrapper over K, typically used in kdb+.

data_types.title: Data Types
data_types.code:
int: 42i
float: 3.14f
char: "a"
str: "hello"
bool: 1b
sym: `hello
date: 2023.01.01
time: 12:00:00.000
data_types.notes: Q introduces distinct scalar types with suffixes (like i, f) and rich temporal types (date, time, timestamp).

operators.title: Operators
operators.code:
sum: 3 + 4
diff: 10 - 5
prod: 2 * 3
quot: 10 % 2

eq: 1 = 1
neq: 1 <> 2
gt: 2 > 1
operators.notes: Evaluation is right-to-left. Division is %. Equality is = and inequality is <>.

conditionals.title: Conditionals
conditionals.notes: cond ($) is used for scalar conditions. The vector conditional (?) operates element-wise over arrays.

for_loop.title: For Loop
for_loop.code:
/ Implicit looping via adverbs like each
squares: {x*x} each til 5

/ Explicit loop
x: 0
do[5; show x; x+:1]
for_loop.notes: til 5 generates 0..4. the 'each' adverb maps the function. 'do' provides an explicit count-based loop.

while_loop.title: While Loop
while_loop.notes: The while loop continues until the condition becomes 0 or false.

functions.title: Functions
functions.notes: Functions are defined in braces. x, y, and z are implicit parameters if not specified in the signature.

arrays.title: Arrays
arrays.code:
vec: 1 2 3 4 5
mat: (1 2 3; 4 5 6)

firstElement: vec 0
count: count vec
arrays.notes: Lists are whitespace-separated. Indexing is zero-based, accessible via juxtaposition or square brackets.

maps.title: Maps
maps.code:
dict: `a`b`c ! 1 2 3
val: dict `b

keysDict: key dict
valsDict: value dict
maps.notes: Dictionaries use the ! operator (bang) between a list of keys and a list of values. Symbols (`) are commonly used as keys.

error_handling.title: Error Handling
error_handling.notes: The protected evaluation operator (@ or .) traps exceptions, passing the error string to a custom handler function.

comments.title: Comments & Headers
comments.code:
# Comment in Q
# Multi-line comments or docstrings
# are documented here
comments.notes: Q uses # or language-specific delimiters (% in MATLAB, ! in Fortran) for comments.

numbers.title: Vectors, Matrices & Numbers
numbers.notes: Q is optimized for vector and matrix calculations with high-precision numerical representations.

booleans.title: Logical Vectors & Booleans
booleans.code:
is_valid = TRUE
flags = c(TRUE, FALSE, TRUE)
booleans.notes: Q provides boolean types with support for element-wise vector logic operations.

type_casting.title: Type Coercion & Casting
type_casting.notes: Q converts data between numeric, character, factor, and logical representations.

strings.title: Strings & Character Vectors
strings.notes: Q treats strings as atomic character scalars or vector arrays.

string_formatting.title: String Formatting
string_formatting.notes: Q formats numerical output with sprintf formatting specifiers.

pattern_matching.title: Conditionals & Switches
pattern_matching.notes: Q executes branch logic via switch, ifelse, or conditional filtering.

range.title: Sequences & Indexing
range.notes: Q indexes matrices and vectors using 1-based indexing and sequence generators.

iterators.title: Vectorized Apply & Iteration
iterators.notes: Q emphasizes vectorized functional processing (apply, map) over explicit loops.

oop_classes.title: Object Systems & S3/S4
oop_classes.code:
# Object systems in Q
obj = list(name = "Model", score = 0.95)
class(obj) = "metric"
oop_classes.notes: Q uses class dispatch systems (S3/S4 in R, multiple dispatch in Julia) for data modeling.

lists.title: DataFrames & Lists
lists.notes: Q stores heterogeneous columnar records in data frames and lists.

tuples.title: Pairs & Records
tuples.notes: Q uses named vectors or lightweight structures for data records.

sets.title: Set Operations
sets.notes: Q provides native mathematical set functions (union, intersect, setdiff).

modules_import.title: Libraries & Packages
modules_import.notes: Q loads package namespaces using library or import declarations.
